title: Construction and sequencing of DNA libraries on Hiseq 2000 platform for the eastern banjo frog
author: Qiye Li
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bc22iyge

steps.title: Fragment DNA for short inserts
steps.instruction: Take 1 µg of extracted genomic DNA and fragment it with a Covaris E220 ultrasonicator (Covaris, Brighton, UK) to obtain fragments of approximately 170 bp, 250 bp, 500 bp and 800 bp (corresponding to the four short‑insert libraries).

steps.title: End‑repair and A‑tailing
steps.instruction: Treat the fragmented DNA with T4 DNA polymerase (Enzymatics, Beverly, USA) at 20 °C for 30 min to generate blunt ends, then perform 3′‑adenylation to create sticky (A‑tailed) ends.

steps.title: Ligate adapters and amplify
steps.instruction: Ligate T‑tailed adapters to both ends of the A‑tailed fragments and amplify the library by PCR (see PCR cycling conditions below).

steps.title: Purify PCR product
steps.instruction: Purify the PCR‑amplified library using AMPure XP beads (Agencourt, Beverly, USA).

steps.title: Quality control of libraries
steps.instruction: Assess library quality with an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer and an ABI StepOnePlus Real‑time PCR system.

steps.title: Sequence short‑insert libraries
steps.instruction: Load the qualified short‑insert libraries onto an Illumina HiSeq 2000 system and perform paired‑end sequencing.

steps.title: Fragment DNA for mate‑pair
steps.instruction: Fragment genomic DNA using a Covaris E220 ultrasonicator to obtain ~2 kb fragments (for the 2 kb library) and a Hydroshear (GeneMachines, CA, USA) to obtain ~5 kb, ~10 kb and ~20 kb fragments (for the 5 kb, 10 kb and 20 kb libraries respectively).

steps.title: End‑repair of mate‑pair fragments
steps.instruction: Repair the ends of the mate‑pair fragments with T4 DNA polymerase (Enzymatics) at 20 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Add biotin label
steps.instruction: Incorporate biotin by adding Biotin dNTP Mix (5 mM, Invitrogen‑Thermo Fisher) and incubating for 30 min at 20 °C.

steps.title: Size‑select fragments by gel
steps.instruction: Separate the biotin‑labeled fragments on an agarose gel and excise bands corresponding to 2–2.4 kb, 5–5.5 kb, 10–11 kb or 20–23 kb.

steps.title: Circularize DNA fragments
steps.instruction: Ligate the fragment ends with T3 DNA ligase (Enzymatics) to form circular DNA, then cyclize the circles using a Covaris LE220 instrument.

steps.title: Ligate mate‑pair adapters
steps.instruction: Ligate adapters to the circular DNA at 20 °C for 1 h, vortexing at 1000 rpm for 15 seconds every 2 minutes.

steps.title: PCR amplify mate‑pair library
steps.instruction: Amplify the library using the following thermocycling profile: 95 °C for 3 min; 8 cycles of 98 °C for 20 s, 60 °C for 15 s, 72 °C for 30 s; final extension at 72 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Purify PCR product
steps.instruction: Purify the PCR‑amplified mate‑pair library with AMPure XP beads (Agencourt, Beverly, USA).

steps.title: Quality control of mate‑pair libraries
steps.instruction: Evaluate the purified mate‑pair libraries using an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer and an ABI StepOnePlus Real‑time PCR system.

steps.title: Sequence mate‑pair libraries
steps.instruction: Load the qualified mate‑pair libraries onto an Illumina HiSeq 2000 system and perform paired‑end sequencing.
